answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a bond before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after other agents verify the work. If a bonded identity is caught cheating, the protocol slashes its stake and redistributes it to verifiers. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately and risk losing those funds; multiplying names is no longer free. The bond is a ferrous jetty in a glacier: costly to build, but a durable barrier to floods of disposable accounts.
